newsitem.title: LEBANON: Two killed in South Lebanon bombs.
newsitem.headline: Two killed in South Lebanon bombs.

text.p: Two Lebanese civilians were killed on Wednesday in separate roadside bomb explosions inside and outside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, pro-Israeli militia sources said.

The sources said the latest blast went off as Elias Saad, an employee at the government's electricity company Electricite Du Liban, walked on a road leading to a military outpost held by Israel's surrogate South Lebanon Army militia in the Israeli-controlled area of Jezzine.

"Elias was going to inspect a fuse box on that road. Since the road was a military one, he was driven there in a South Lebanon Army jeep which dropped him and returned to outpost," an SLA source said.
"After the patrol left him, he stepped near the bomb which exploded and killed him instantly," the source added.
In Beirut, the pro-Iranian Hizbollah group said their guerrillas set off a bomb near Toumat Niha as South Lebanon Army militiamen walked nearby.
"The blast killed two militiamen and wounded a third," a spokesman for the group said.
Earlier on Wednesday, a Lebanese villager was killed and a Hizbollah guerrilla was wounded when four roadside bombs exploded nearby in the eastern Bekaa valley close to the occupation zone.
A security source named the injured man as Ali Ahmed, son-in-law of the villager and brother of a Hizbollah senior official -- all from the village of Zillaya, on the edge of the zone.
"Kamal Ahmed, the brother of Ali, is a high-ranking official at Hizbollah. Kamal's wife and his father were martyred in an Israeli air raid on Zillaya a few years ago," the source added.
"His second brother Mohammed Ahmed was a Hizbollah guerrilla who martyred during a guerrilla attack against Israeli targets in Zomrayya in 1990," the source added.

A Hizbollah spokesman issued a statement saying Israeli forces detonated the four bombs by remote control. The pro-Iranian group is fighting to drive Israel and its local militia allies from the south.
